name: Vinotonus

attributes.attribute: name may include the syllable for wine
shrine on the Yorkshire moors as a god of wild nature
compared by Roman soldiers to Silvanus

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Vinotonus is a British god. His name may point to wine, since it holds the syllable vin. A shrine to him stands on the Yorkshire moors. There he stands as a deity of unchained wildness, and Roman soldiers read him as their wood god Silvanus. The twin ties may rest on the wild conduct of those who drink wine, or the wine link may be a mistaken reading of his name.

okr.objective: Present Vinotonus as a British god of wild nature honored on the Yorkshire moors.
key_results: A shrine to Vinotonus sits on the Yorkshire moors.
Roman soldiers linked him with the god Silvanus.
His name may derive from the word for wine.
